arxiv-2112-08667.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Haley M. Cole, Michael B. Venuti, Brian Gorman, Eric D. Bauer, Mun K. Chan, Serena Eley. In type-II superconductors exposed to magnetic fields between upper and lower critical values, H c ​ 1 H_{c1} and H c ​ 2 H_{c2} , penetrating magnetic flux forms a lattice of vortices whose motion can induce dissipation. Consequently, the magnetization M M of superconductors is typically progressively weakened with increasing magnetic field B ∝ n v B\propto n_{v} (for vortex density n v n_{v} ).

pmc-11452944.creator: Leiming Wang, Lei Cheng, Yongjuan Fu, Hua Dong, Yanlei Xiong, Dehong Lu, Yueshan Piao, Lianghong Teng
pmc-11452944.description: 2]. Supratentorial ependymomas (ST-EPNs) are primarily characterized by two types of fusion variations involving the zinc finger translocation-associated gene (ZFTA) and Yes1-Associated Transcriptional regulator (YAP1) [2]. ZFTA fusion occurs in approximately 66–84% of pediatric ST-EPNs and generally indicates a poor prognosis. In contrast, YAP1 fusion is relatively rare (6–7% of pediatric cases) and usually suggests a more indolent biological behavior.

uslaw-usc-t14-s2157.description: United States Code, Title 14 (Coast Guard); Chapter 21 (Personnel; Officers); Subchapter II (Discharges; Retirements; Revocation Of Commissions; Separation For Cause). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. During any period in which the Coast Guard is not operating as a service in the Navy, section 1216(d) of title 10 does not apply with respect to flag officers of the Coast Guard.

uslaw-usc-t38-s7426.title: 38 U.S.C. § 7426 — Retirement rights
uslaw-usc-t38-s7426.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t38-s7426.description: United States Code, Title 38 (Veterans’ Benefits); Part V (Boards, Administrations, And Services); Chapter 74 (Veterans Health Administration—Personnel); Subchapter II (Collective Bargaining And Personnel Administration). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Except as provided in subsection (b), persons appointed to the Administration shall be subject to the provisions of and entitled to benefits under subchapter III of chapter 83 of title 5.
